cards.text: Moses is still preaching to Israel, walking them back through the whole journey. They've just beaten two kings, Sihon and Og, on the east side of the Jordan River (Deuteronomy 2:32-3:3). Now Moses says, "So at that time we took possession of this land."

Then Moses hands out the land: Reuben and Gad get the stretch from the Arnon Valley up to the Jabbok River, and the half-tribe of Manasseh gets the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan. One man from Manasseh, Jair, renames Bashan after himself: Havvoth-jair. The Millers carved my name on a HANDLE. Jair put his on a whole REGION.
But here's the catch. The LORD has given these tribes their land, and Moses still has an order for their men of valor.

cards.question: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh already have their land east of the Jordan. What does Moses command their fighting men to do?

answers.text: Cross over armed ahead of their brothers
Stay behind and guard their new cities
Build a wall along the Jordan River

cards.question: True or false: The fighting men's wives, children and livestock have to cross the Jordan with them.

cards.text: Right in the middle of battle orders, Moses slips in, "…I know that you have much livestock…" That's your buddy helping you move, stopping to say, "I know you've got a LOT of boxes."

cards.question: Moses says the families and herds stay in those cities until the LORD gives ___ to their brothers, as He has to them.
Once their brothers have taken their land across the Jordan, what may each of these fighting men do?

answers.text: Return to the land Moses gave him
Pick new land on the west side
Stay on to serve under Joshua

cards.text: Then Moses turns to Joshua, his attendant (Exodus 24:13), and tells him, "Your own eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings." And Moses says the LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms Joshua is about to enter.

cards.question: Moses tells Joshua not to be afraid of the kingdoms he's about to enter. Why not?

answers.text: The LORD Himself will fight for him
Israel's army is far bigger than theirs

cards.text: Then Moses tells Israel he pleaded with the LORD. Not asked, friend. PLEADED. He prays, "O Lord GOD, You have begun to show Your greatness and power to Your servant."

cards.question: Moses has seen God's mighty works up close. What does he ask the LORD for?

answers.text: To cross over and see the good land
To defeat one more king in battle
To see the face of the LORD

cards.text: But Moses tells the people the LORD was angry with him on account of them. And He would not listen to him.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD tells Moses he can bring this request up again later.

cards.text: The LORD still has more to say. He sends Moses somewhere: up to the top of Pisgah.

cards.question: Moses is headed to the top of Pisgah. What does the LORD tell him to do up there?

answers.text: Look over the land in every direction
Pray for the people camped below
Build an altar out of the stones

cards.question: True or false: The LORD tells Moses he will not cross the Jordan.

cards.text: I think that one hurts, friend. But the LORD isn't finished with Moses yet, and He has one more order.

cards.question: Moses won't be crossing the Jordan. What is the LORD's last order for him here?
Joshua will cross over ahead of the people and help them ___ the land that Moses will see.

cards.text: So Moses and Israel stay in the valley opposite Beth-peor. That's where we'll pause, friend, but trust me, Moses isn't done preaching.
